lede: At the early 13:00 New York close the S&P 500 rose 1.6% to 7,297.49, the Nasdaq Composite gained 2.31% to 24,129.50 and the Dow Jones Industrial Average added 1.18% to 50,774.94, Bloomberg and CNBC reported. Bloomberg said traders bought beaten-down technology shares, lifting the Nasdaq 100 by 2.6%. Vertex Pharmaceuticals fell after the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) pushed its decision on a kidney drug into 2027. Euro area consumers raise their one-year inflation expectation to 3.5% in October from 3.1%, a European Central Bank survey shows, while French inflation slows to 2.9% and Spanish inflation to 4.1% in November.

items.title: Wall Street rallies in shortened session; S&P 500 gains 1.6% to 7,297.49
facts: The S&P 500 rose 1.6% to 7,297.49 and the Nasdaq Composite rose 2.31% to 24,129.50 at the early 13:00 New York close on November 27, CNBC reported.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 591.99 points, or 1.18%, to 50,774.94, according to CNBC.
CNBC reported that the Dow Jones Industrial Average had its best week since October 2022 and the S&P 500 its best since April 2025, after a correction earlier in November.
items.why: The rebound lifts US stock benchmarks off November's correction lows heading into December, with technology leading.

items.title: Traders buy battered tech shares as the Nasdaq 100 climbs 2.6%
facts: The Nasdaq 100 rose 2.6% on November 27 as traders bought technology shares that fell hard in November's selloff, Bloomberg reported.
Bloomberg said trading in New York ended early, at 13:00, because of the day after the Thanksgiving holiday.
items.why: Technology and chip stocks led the rally, so the tech-heavy indexes beat the broader market in the holiday-thinned session.

items.title: Micron and Qualcomm rise more than 5% as chip stocks rebound
facts: Micron Technology and Qualcomm each gained more than 5% on November 27, CNBC reported.
CNBC said the chip sector rebounded from a heavy selloff earlier in the week, and Sandisk rose 15.96% to lead the S&P 500.
items.why: The rebound in memory and chip makers drove the Nasdaq Composite's gain as investors went back into the artificial intelligence (AI) trade.

items.title: Vertex falls 8% as US regulator pushes kidney drug decision to 2027
facts: Vertex Pharmaceuticals shares fell as much as 8% on November 27, Bloomberg reported.
The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) pushed its decision on the kidney drug povetacicept into 2027, Bloomberg reported, after it asked for more information late in the review.
items.why: The delay pushes back a new revenue source for Vertex and weighed on health care, the weakest-performing sector of the session.

items.title: Newmont gains 4.1% as gold miners rise with metal prices
facts: Newmont rose 4.1% on November 27 as miners climbed with higher metal prices, CNBC reported at midday.
AngloGold Ashanti added 4.7%, according to CNBC.
items.why: Higher gold prices lifted mining shares and helped materials rank among the session's strongest sectors.

items.title: Skydance ends $4.0 billion receivables facility after repaying $3.9 billion
facts: Skydance Corporation said a subsidiary repaid all $3.9 billion outstanding and ended its $4.0 billion receivables purchase agreement, with PNC Bank as agent, on November 20.
On November 25, the company sent redemption notices for several of its notes due in 2027, which it will redeem at 100% of principal plus accrued interest.
items.why: Repaying the facility and the 2027 notes reduces the media group's near-term debt maturities, which matters for its bonds and credit ratings.

items.title: Block agrees to pay $442.5 million to settle shareholder class action
facts: In a November 27 filing, Block said it agreed in principle to pay $442.5 million to settle a federal securities class action brought by shareholders.
The proposed settlement still needs approval from a federal judge.
items.why: A one-time cost for the payments company that, once approved, ends a major lawsuit hanging over its shares.

items.title: EU clears Deutsche Börse's €5.3 billion takeover of Allfunds
facts: The European Commission approved Deutsche Börse's purchase of the fund distribution platform Allfunds without conditions after a first-phase review, MLex reported on November 27.
MLex, citing the regulator, put the deal's value at €5.3 billion ($6.1 billion).
items.why: Removes the EU antitrust hurdle to the exchange operator's fund services deal, which matters for Deutsche Börse and Allfunds shares in Europe.

items.title: Carnival moves up the end of its CEO's 2022 performance award by one year
facts: On November 24, the compensation committee of Carnival's board amended a 2022 special performance-based stock unit grant held by Chief Executive Officer Josh Weinstein.
The award's performance period now ends on November 30, 2026 instead of November 30, 2027, so it vests in December 2026.
items.why: The cruise operator's CEO award now settles a year early, which brings forward its share issuance and pay expense.

items.title: Viatris director W. Don Cornwell retires from board effective December 1
facts: W. Don Cornwell told Viatris on November 23 that he will retire from its board of directors, effective December 1, 2026.
The drugmaker reported his retirement in a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) on November 27.
items.why: A change to the generic drugmaker's board; it does not touch its guidance or capital plans.

items.title: Euro area consumers lift one-year inflation expectations to 3.5% in October
facts: Median expected inflation over the next 12 months rises to 3.5% in October from 3.1% in September, the European Central Bank's Consumer Expectations Survey shows.
Three-year-ahead expectations edge up to 3.0% from 2.9%; five-year-ahead expectations hold at 2.5%, the highest since the series began in August 2022.
Perceived inflation over the past 12 months climbs to 4.1%, the highest since July 2024, while expected income growth falls to 0.6% from 1.1%.
items.why: Higher household inflation expectations add to the case for tighter European Central Bank policy, bearing on short-dated euro area bond yields and the euro.

items.title: French consumer price inflation slows to 2.9% in November
facts: Consumer prices rise 2.9% from a year earlier in November after 3.4% in October, the national statistics office INSEE estimates; prices fall 0.7% on the month.
Energy inflation eases to 19.2% from 24.1% on cheaper petroleum products, while fresh food prices rise 9.4% from a year earlier.
The EU-harmonised index of consumer prices (HICP) rises 3.2% year on year; INSEE publishes final November figures on December 11.
items.why: A softer reading from the euro area's second-largest economy feeds into the December 1 euro area flash estimate and European Central Bank rate pricing.

items.title: Spanish inflation eases to 4.1% in November on cheaper fuel
facts: Consumer prices rise 4.1% from a year earlier in November, down from 4.9% in October, the National Statistics Institute (INE) flash estimate shows.
Core inflation falls 0.5 percentage point to 2.6%, as fuel prices for private vehicles drop compared with a rise in November 2025.
The EU-harmonised index rises 4.1% on the year and falls 0.7% on the month; harmonised core inflation stands at 2.7%.
items.why: Spain's slowdown, together with France's, points to energy-driven easing ahead of the euro area flash inflation figure, touching euro area bond yields.

items.title: French economy shrinks 0.2% in third quarter, revised from 0.1% drop
facts: Gross domestic product (GDP) falls 0.2% in the third quarter after no growth in the second, INSEE says, down from its first estimate of a 0.1% decline.
Foreign trade subtracts 0.6 percentage point from growth as exports drop sharply.
Household purchasing power rises 0.2% per consumption unit after a 0.5% fall; the savings rate holds at 17.4% of gross disposable income.
items.why: A contracting French economy with inflation near 3% bears on French government bond spreads and on the European Central Bank's growth assessment.

items.title: China's industrial profits rise 20.1% in October
facts: Chinese industrial profits rise 20.1% from a year earlier in October, up from 14.4% in September, National Bureau of Statistics data show.
Profits for January through October total 6.74 trillion yuan, up 16.0% from the same period of 2025.
Electronics makers contribute 9.7 percentage points to the 10-month gain, bureau statistician Yu Weining says; high-tech manufacturing profits rise 50.9%.
items.why: Profit gains concentrated in electronics favor Chinese technology hardware suppliers and support demand for industrial metals.
